brief:
Design an extraordinary contemporary Caribbean waterfront estate in Saint Lucia with an estimated property value of US$25 million, approximately six generous bedroom suites, expansive living and entertainment spaces, a memorable entrance, exceptional indoor-outdoor connections, substantial shaded terraces and a rectangular swimming pool.

Aim for sophisticated luxury architecture: a clear architectural idea, hierarchy of primary and subordinate volumes, beautiful proportions, privacy, climatic shading, considered facade depth, coordinated materials and compelling arrival and waterfront elevations. Resolve individual suite allocations, social and service accommodation and actual connected circulation rather than relying on room-capacity labels.

You have creative freedom over composition, spatial organization, number of levels, entrance relationships, roof forms and building arrangement within the canonical compiler's documented capabilities. No three-pavilion arrangement, fixed roof style or predefined mansion template is required. Select your own architectural decisions; the deterministic compiler calculates supported geometry, shared boundaries, openings, floors and stairs.

This experiment requests the supported editable architectural envelope, not complete fit-out, landscaping, terrain or marine engineering. Use the documented flat-site representation; ocean context is conceptual. Lawn/bed surfaces are sufficient landscape reserves; planting and grading are outside this test. A rectangular pool is requested, not an unsupported infinity-edge amenity. Do not claim those unsupported features are constructed.

Use the extended canonical contract faithfully. If your intended architectural decision is unsupported, preserve and disclose that decision or return decision-required; never silently replace it with ordinary rectangles. Do not omit programme or flatten ambitious design merely to claim completion. The resulting architecture will be judged in aerial, arrival, garden and poolside views, separately from schema acceptance and construction fidelity.

plan.thesis: A terraced Caribbean courtyard estate recast as a landward arrival bar and elevated guest belvedere framing a long, shaded waterward social sequence. The composition distinguishes a tall ivory arrival/gallery spine, limestone private wings with individually resolved suites, and low bronze-roofed service and outdoor entertaining elements. A compact upper guest-and-owner belvedere gives the arrival elevation and waterfront silhouette sectional hierarchy without turning the estate into a repetitive pavilion field. The south-facing pool terrace remains the primary waterfront room; screens and recessed openings provide selective shade and privacy rather than glazing every facade.

output.concept: Water Court Estate: a single-storey, climate-responsive waterfront residence composed as a ceremonial north arrival court, a central ivory gallery spine, and a broad water-facing salon under a disciplined sequence of low flat bronze roofs. Two deliberately unequal-feeling but proportionally matched private suite cloisters extend east and west from the gallery, creating privacy without repeating detached pavilions. Shaded dining and living terraces form the south waterfront threshold to a rectangular pool and lawn reserve. The US$25 million figure is treated only as an ambition reference, not as a construction-cost or valuation claim.

plan.thesis: A contemporary Caribbean water court organized as a memorable landward arrival threshold and calm gallery procession to a generous shaded waterfront salon. A limestone-and-timber private cloister on each side shelters six individually allocated suites, while the ivory social volume opens to paired roofed terraces, pool and lawn. The composition uses a limited material palette, deep shaded outdoor rooms and selective exterior glazing rather than continuous glass.

addressed.response: Redesigned the plan around a short central gallery and two controlled 20 m cloister halls; suite cells now terminate beyond the salon’s east and west edges rather than crossing its footprint.
Moved the arrival planting reserve north of the forecourt and increased the flat-site envelope to contain arrival landscape, pool and waterfront lawn.
Re-authored all circulation relationships with shared-wall portals and limited fixed windows to known outer suite and lounge facades; incompatible interior-facing windows were removed.
Adopted separated, overhang-free flat roof plates throughout, avoiding unconstructible eave intersections and preserving a calm contemporary roof hierarchy.
Removed partial upper stacking and all pitched roofs, so every roofed space receives an independent flat roof without lean-to or valley conditions.
Placed the two timber privacy screens only on exposed suite façades and offset them from the centred fixed windows.

Every interior space now has a declared portal sequence from the arrival forecourt through entry, gallery, cloister halls or service rooms; the isolated upper rooms were removed in the single-storey redesign.

changes.change: Replaced the prior mixed-height belvedere and repetitive suite-bar arrangement with a single-level water-court plan.
changes.reason: Creates a clearer Caribbean arrival-to-waterfront sequence while eliminating the collision, isolated upper circulation and partial roof conditions.

changes.change: Consolidated nine sleeping rooms and separate bathroom cells into six generous self-contained suites arranged on two cloister halls.
changes.reason: Meets the approximately six-suite brief without repetitive bedroom-and-bath cell stacks; each suite explicitly includes private bathroom allocation.

changes.change: Established a single ceremonial entry-gallery-social axis with shared portals to both suite cloisters and service rooms.
changes.reason: Ensures actual connected arrival circulation to every interior allocation.

changes.change: Changed relationship openings to shared-wall declarations and restricted glazing/screens to exposed external facades.
changes.reason: Avoids interior-facing windows, pier conflicts and screens obstructing doors.

changes.change: Changed all roofed spaces to independent flat roof plates with no overhangs.
changes.reason: The supported flat roof strategy cleanly resolves every adjacent volume and roofed terrace.

changes.change: Retained two roofed terraces but strengthened their role as a continuous waterfront threshold to the rectangular pool and lawn.
changes.reason: Preserves substantial shaded outdoor living and clarifies the poolside experience.

retained: A memorable roofed arrival forecourt and ceremonial entry sequence.
A broad water-facing principal living salon with separate dining and evening entertainment rooms.
Six generous private bedroom suites, each with sleeping, dressing and private bathroom allocation.
Dedicated entertaining kitchen, pantry, laundry and service store.
Two substantial shaded terraces, a rectangular swimming pool and lawn/bed landscape reserves.
Ivory, limestone, timber and bronze material character with selective climatic timber screening.
Flat-site representation and conceptual waterfront orientation only.
limitations: The plan authors the supported editable architectural envelope only; it does not include full interior fit-out, planting, trees, grading, marine works, shoreline engineering, stormwater design, hurricane engineering, corrosion engineering, guards or structural design.
The waterfront and ocean outlook are conceptual because no surveyed shore, flood elevation, setbacks or environmental permissions were supplied.
Pool is a supported rectangular basin; no infinity edge, catch basin or marine amenity is claimed.
Landscape entries are lawn and bed ground-surface reserves only, not planting designs.
No construction budget, cost allocation or market valuation is asserted from the US$25 million estimated property-value reference.

scalars.from: A terraced Caribbean courtyard estate recast as a landward arrival bar and elevated guest belvedere framing a long, shaded waterward social sequence. The composition distinguishes a tall ivory arrival/gallery spine, limestone private wings with individually resolved suites, and low bronze-roofed service and outdoor entertaining elements. A compact upper guest-and-owner belvedere gives the arrival elevation and waterfront silhouette sectional hierarchy without turning the estate into a repetitive pavilion field. The south-facing pool terrace remains the primary waterfront room; screens and recessed openings provide selective shade and privacy rather than glazing every facade.
